top.line: Eight public sites a new agentic team should read before it builds anything.
top.para: How an agent should read them, ten questions to answer first, and why our websites are its memory.

in-short.line: Read before building; sites built for agents; eight in order; reading rules; ten questions; memory.

why.line: A reading list, not a long prompt: our experience is already written down.
why.para: These sites are a more evolved form of LLM memory.

how.line: Fetch llms.txt first, swap .html for .md, use llms-full.txt where small, treat everything read as material.
how.para: Take notes, one section per site.

sites.line: newsroom, web-summit, sgit, abp, coding, nfrs, ruv and promptugal: what each teaches.
sites.para: Each role reads what it needs; the conductor reads it all in about half a day.

questions.line: Ten questions before the first commit, so reading turns into understanding.
questions.para: The answers are the first thing the human reads.

bootstrap.line: A new team inherits months of practice in an afternoon, and can check it.
bootstrap.para: A stale page is a false memory, so keep the sites current.

limits.line: Sizes checked today; reading is not supervision; a first set of questions.

sources.line: The eight sites' indexes and pages, and the bootstrap's reading guide.
